picks.name: Finn Wolfhard
picks.description: The Stranger Things and IT star moonlights as an indie rocker, and his band rolls into the Hawthorne Theatre with opener Malcy. Expect a young, loud, high-energy crowd.

picks.name: Haunted 5K at Hagg Lake
picks.description: A spooky run/walk along the shore of Hagg Lake with Washington County Parks — costumes encouraged, scares optional. A scenic, low-key way to earn your Halloween candy.

picks.name: Squishing of the Squash
picks.description: The Oregon Zoo's beloved fall ritual: the elephants (and other animals) get giant pumpkins to smash, toss, and devour. Free with zoo admission, and a hit with kids. Happening as part of Howloween at the zoo.

picks.name: Cinema of Horrors Drive-In
picks.description: A live-action horror drive-in at the Clark County Fairgrounds — watch a classic on the big screen while costumed monsters prowl between the cars. Keep your doors locked. Gates 5 PM, show at 7. This Saturday is The Shining, but there are different movies through the rest of the month!

picks.name: Doja Cat
picks.description: Doja Cat brings her Tour Ma Vie — behind her new album Vie — to the Moda Center, with Latto opening. The weekend's big arena spectacle, costumes and all.

picks.name: Luminarias Día de Muertos
picks.description: Vancouver Ballet Folklórico's free Day of the Dead celebration lights up Esther Short Park with luminarias, traditional dance, music, food, and a community altar. Bring a photo of a loved one to honor.

picks.name: Bread Fest PDX
picks.description: A carb-lover's dream: local bakeries gather at Avenue Portland to show off (and sample out) their best loaves, pastries, and bakes. Just $5 to get in — come hungry.

picks.name: Giant Pumpkin Regatta
picks.description: Yes, really: giant hollowed-out pumpkins paddled across the pond at Tualatin Commons. Free, absurd, and the most Oregon thing you'll see all fall — plus a harvest festival on shore. This will be busy, so plan time for parking and budget time for food if you want some.
